name: Weblium
summary: Template-based website builder for small businesses, with an AI assistant, lead capture forms and integrations, and an online store, blog and multilingual pages on the Business plan.
best_for: small businesses and freelancers who want a template-based site with forms and integrations for one business, at a low yearly price
skip_if: you need many sites under one subscription, a large content site on Starter, or full design and code control
honest_knock: Starter caps a site at 10 pages and 5 GB of bandwidth and has no blog or online store; those need Business. Every subscription covers one website, and moving to a cheaper plan only works after the current term ends. The Free plan is limited to 3 pages, 100 MB storage and 100 MB bandwidth, and a Free site goes offline 46 days after its 14-day trial and is deleted 60 days after that. During the trial a site cannot be indexed, connect a domain or show form replies in readable form. Weblium's own savings figures disagree: the pricing page claims up to 67% off for paying yearly, its FAQ and the September 2026 pricing post say up to 30%, and the bundle help article from 2024 says up to 50% against 25-40% on the pricing page.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month billed yearly ($132 a year), one website
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-08 on weblium.com/pricing in a browser render, USD; the FAQ says all prices are in USD) Three plans, each for one website. Free has the editor, 300+ templates, mobile optimisation, free icons and photos and the Evo AI assistant, with up to 3 pages per site, 100 MB storage and 100 MB bandwidth and no credit card; the Free card's '60 days' label is how long a free site stays online, explained below. Starter is $11 a month billed annually ($132 a year) or $16 billed monthly ($192 a year): advanced SEO settings, lead capture tools, advanced design, integrations and custom code, up to 10 pages per site, 3 GB media storage, 5 GB bandwidth and no Weblium branding. Business, marked most popular, is $17.50 a month annually ($210 a year) or $25 monthly ($300 a year) and adds the online store, the blog, multilingual sites in up to 5 languages, up to 500 pages, 10 GB storage and 20 GB bandwidth. Starter and Business have a 14-day free trial without a card. Each subscription covers one website; bundles for 5, 10 or 15 sites save 25-40%. Annual plans include a free domain for the first year. You can upgrade any time, but to move to a lower plan you cancel auto-renewal and buy the new plan after the current one ends. If a renewal payment fails, paid features stay on for 5 days and the site then drops to Free. Weblium Studio builds sites for you from $300, and a white-label version for agencies starts at $48 a month. Re-read on 25 October 2026 with a plain fetch: plan contents and the FAQ amounts ($132 and $210 a year, $16 and $25 a month) unchanged; the bundle prices on the cards render only in a browser. Weblium's changelog explains the 60 days. In the pricing update dated 2 September 2026, which it calls its first major pricing update in seven years, the old Free and Pro plans became Free, Starter and Business, and a Free website now stays live for up to 60 days. A new site starts with a 14-day trial, then stays on Free for 46 days before it goes offline; its data is kept for another 60 days and then deleted permanently. The help article comparing the plans (updated 31 July 2026) adds that a Free site is not indexed by search engines, cannot connect a domain or use contact forms, and that an account can hold up to three Free sites at a time.

compare_with.name: Webflow
compare_with.why: Webflow is in our dossiers too and gives designers far more control over layout, CMS and code, at higher prices. Weblium is the simpler template builder: cheaper per site, but with page caps and the blog and store only on Business.

exit_test.what: Created two draft products manually, exported them, and updated the second description through an ID-preserving CSV reimport.
exit_test.awkward: The initial custom CSV import produced no products or message; its cause is unknown and is not counted as data loss. Product amounts were entered in the store currency USD although the kit uses EUR. Description line structure is represented by HTML blocks, and price formatting drops the trailing zero. The export dialog warns that attached files, images and old URLs are excluded.

friction.export_route: Your Store > Products > select the two test products > Export > Selected products > Plain CSV > Download CSV.
friction.format: UTF-8 CSV without BOM. Descriptions contain HTML, prices use a decimal point, and Visibility is no.
friction.reimport: Reimport retained the same slug IDs and variants. Only the second description changed; the first record and all other parsed fields remained identical, with no duplicates.
friction.cancellation: Cancellation, expiry and account deletion were not tested. The control date, where recorded, is planning only.

not_tested: Full signup screen count and first-result setup speed.
All kit fields that were not entered.
came_along: Both products, Unicode names, SKUs, quantities and slug IDs are present in both exports. Descriptions retain their text as HTML spans. Numeric prices are unchanged.
exit_test.note: One export and re-import of synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We started an unpublished shop from a template, added two made-up products, exported them, imported a changed copy and looked at the plans.
findings: The trial runs on the Business plan for 14 days; Free is 'Free for 60 days', not forever. Starter is $16 and Business $25 a month, or $11 and $17.50 billed yearly. No card was asked.
Products save as drafts ('Your site visitors can't see it yet'), and the site stays unpublished until you click Publish.
The product export is a plain CSV. The export screen warns that attached files, images and old URLs are not exported.
Our two products came back with names, accents, SKU and stock intact. Prices lost a trailing zero (12.10 became 12.1), and the description came back wrapped in HTML.
Re-importing the export with one description changed updated that product in place: still two products, the same IDs, and nothing else changed.
Our first import, built from scratch in the export's format, finished without any message and added nothing. We added the products by hand instead.
not_tested: Images and other attachments in the export
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
